entry.summary: A visa is needed to travel to Liberia.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The Liberian dollar is the official currency, however, the US dollar is accepted as legal tender. Liberia’s banking sector may experience cash shortages (of both US and Liberian dollars). Bring sufficient cash, in US dollars, to cover all expenses. Banks and foreign exchange facilities may be unable to pay out transferred funds or fulfil ATM withdrawals. ATMs are limited in Monrovia, and only allow cash withdrawals using a Visa card. consular.notes: Australia doesn't have an embassy or consulate in Liberia. You can get consular help from the Australian High Commission in Accra, Ghana. The Australian High Commission in Accra currently has very limited capacity to provide consular assistance in West Africa, except in Ghana.

laws.rule: It's a serious offence to have, use or traffic illegal drugs. Penalties can include large fines and long jail terms. Don't bring drugs into Liberia. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are illegal, with penalties up to one year in prison. - Advice for LGBTQIA+ travellers
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ laws

laws.rule: It's illegal to: have pornographic material take photos around military and government buildings, airports, seaports, bridges and important government buildings export diamonds, unless you follow local export laws Penalties can be severe. Local prison conditions are harsh. - Staying within the law
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You can drive in Liberia for up to 12 months with an International Driving Permit (IDP). You will also need to carry a police cover note in addition to your IDP. You must get your IDP before you leave Australia. After 12 months, you need a Liberian licence to drive.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Liberia is a conservative society, especially in areas outside Monrovia. Think about your clothing choices. Local women wear loose-fitting clothes that cover the upper arms and legs.
